    Saturation with respect to an idempotent coordinate #

    For a left module M and an idempotent coordinate e, the largest submodule on which the entire left ideal generated by e acts trivially consists of the elements x satisfying (e * r) • x = 0 for every scalar r.

    Applied to M / L, its inverse image in M is the source-literal maximal enlargement of L that is invisible to the projective coordinate R e. This is the elementary saturation operation used in Iyama's realization argument.

    (∀ (f : P →ₗ[R] M), f = 0) ↔ ∀ (g : Q →ₗ[R] M), g = 0

    Universal vanishing of linear maps is unchanged when the source is replaced by a linearly equivalent module.
